text:
maya: ACME just sent hard targets — p95 50ms, p99 200ms at 5k qps for chat completions. They want this in contract. Thoughts?

juan: Not realistic on shared pool without carveouts. Our profiler shows KV cold misses and kernel fallbacks dominate the p99.

sasha: We can hit p95~50ms on A100 with microbatch=1 + fused_attn kernel, but qps suffers (you need more nodes). p99 still spikes if KV hit_rate < ~0.9.

maya: Can you paste the quick numbers from the perf run?

juan: Sure — local run (1000 requests):
```
config: model=redwood-xl-13b, seq=512
microbatch=1 kernel=fused_attn p95=48ms p99=230ms qps=1200
microbatch=4 kernel=default     p95=78ms p99=305ms qps=4200
kv_hit_rate=0.72 (no prewarm)
```

oliver-pm: Sales says ACME will pay for reserved capacity if we can promise p99≤200ms. They asked product for a firm answer today.

carol-sales: Yep. Customer is willing to pay but wants contractual SLA. They expect a proof-of-performance.

maya: Two levers: 1) dedicated/reserved pool for ACME so we can tune microbatch and kernel aggressively, 2) prefix/KV prewarm to raise kv_hit_rate. If kv_hit_rate -> 0.95, p99 drops a lot.

juan: Prewarm script + cache priming helps but needs coordination with their client behavior (long context sessions). Also risk: kernel fused_attn v3 had a regression last week under certain seq lengths (deploy-bot flagged it).

deploy-bot: perf-regression-detector: Regression detected on kernel fused_attn v3 -> v4 in canary: p99 +60ms at seq=1024, microbatch=1. See job 2026-03-15-22.

sasha: Given the regression risk, propose this plan:
- Offer ACME an opt-in reserved pool (dedicated) tuned for microbatch=1 + fused_attn, with explicit kernel version pinned.
- Run a 48h perf validation with KV prewarm and prefix cache enabled; measure p95/p99 at target QPS.
- Canary routing option: 10% traffic to prewarm nodes first, then ramp.

oliver-pm: That sounds reasonable. Sales needs two data points: (A) expected infra size and monthly cost for reserved pool (B) empirical p95/p99 from our 48h validation.

carol-sales: I'll tell ACME we can do reserved pool + validation. Can you produce an internal doc with exact SLO carveouts and fallbacks we propose? They may insist on a hard p99 200ms.

maya: Draft SLO carveout we can offer:
- Standard: p95 ≤ 100ms, p99 ≤ 400ms on shared pool.
- Reserved (opt-in): p95 ≤ 60ms, p99 ≤ 200ms at committed QPS with pinned kernel and prewarm.
- Fallback: if reserved pool unavailable, auto-fallback to a smaller model (latency OK, quality reduced) or reduced payload.

juan: Add runbook items: KV warmup script, microbatch tuning steps, kernel-version pinning, and perf-monitoring alerts for p99 drift. Also include a rollback plan if fused_attn shows regressions.

sasha: Implementation note: to reach kv_hit_rate>0.95 we need either long-lived sessions or an explicit priming endpoint customers call when session starts. Could add a short-life <100 token prefix cache.

oliver-pm: Sales asks for timeline. How long to run the 48h validation and a clear cost estimate?

maya: I can run the validation today against a staging dedicated pool. Need infra allocation (2x expected prod nodes) and @juan to pin kernels. ETA: results by EOD tomorrow.

juan: I'll pin kernel to fused_attn v3 on that pool and add perf-monitoring. Also will run a regression sweep across seq=128/512/1024.

carol-sales: :thumbsup: I'll communicate the plan to ACME and frame the reserved pool as contractual add-on. Keep me posted on the empirical numbers.

sasha: One more thing — for contract wording we should be explicit about traffic shape: p99 guarantees only apply at agreed steady-state QPS and session patterns (startup spikes excluded).

maya: Agreed. I'll include traffic-shape appendix and an acceptance test (client runs 30m synthetic load pattern) as proof-of-performance.

juan: Adding final note — if customer insists on p99≤200ms on shared pool at 5k qps, we should refuse; either reserved pool or a relaxed p99. Otherwise we'll be under-provisioned or face huge cost.

oliver-pm: Understood. I'll sync with Sales leadership and ask ACME if they want reserved capacity.

maya: I'll open a perf run ticket and share logs here when done.

juan: Added to runbook: "kv-warmup.sh --session-prefix" and microbatch tuning matrix.

carol-sales: Thanks team — will loop back after ACME reply.

maya: Thanks all.
